entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

Step 2 is under way. Status at **17:10** (23 minutes in):

- **Baseline**: build passes, 375 tests pass, `dist-server` copied to the scratchpad (471 files).
- **Probe**: one `checkJs` run over the 60 files — 1,947 errors in 16,966 lines, split per file. It took 13 of the allowed 15 minutes; nothing was edited or renamed.
- **Sub-agents**: all six started in one step at 17:02, each with a written brief. Eight files have been renamed so far, and the first whole-tree snapshot shows no errors outside the sets.

Three things the probe turned up that `CLAUDE.md` doesn't cover, and that I built into the briefs:

| Finding | What I did |
|---|---|
| Five already-converted files use typedefs of set files as real types (`podcastUtils.RssPodcastEpisode`, `Audnexus.AuthorSearchObj`, `iTunes.iTunesPodcastSearchResult`) | Briefs require those names to stay importable via a type-only `declare namespace` (precedent `LogManager.ts`); I tested that this also compiles for a module that exports a plain object |
| `semver`, `ssrf-req-filter` and `xml2js` have no type declarations, and only I may edit `server/types/` | Each sub-agent gets a private no-emit config plus a `pending.d.ts` in its scratch folder, so it can validate a proposed declaration without touching the repo; I copy them in during Step 3 |
| `utils/index.js` (40 importers) and `fileUtils.js` (37) change types under all five other sets when converted | Set 5 is told to convert them early and not after 17:30 |

I'm now waiting on the sub-agents. Timers will wake me at 17:27 and 17:43 for whole-tree snapshots (so I can warn a sub-agent that breaks a file outside the sets), at 17:58 after their stop time, and at 18:06 before the 80-minute cutoff.

No correction needed — set 5 is restoring files for sound reasons, not because of my brief:

- `zipHelpers`: the vendored `archiver` lib is inferred as a type that a single-step cast can't reach (TS2352 demands `as unknown as`, which is banned).

- `utils/index.js`: its scratch experiment shows it found the real trap.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `utils/index.js` has arrow functions at module scope that call `this.isObject(…)`. In CommonJS, top-level `this` **is** `module.exports`, and arrow functions capture it. Today that works because `module.exports.isObject = …` populates that same object.
- Convert the file to a trailing `export = { … }` and TypeScript emits `module.exports = { … }` — a *new* object. The arrows still hold the *old* one, which no longer has `isObject` on it. The code compiles, the require shape looks identical, and it throws at runtime.
- So the 40-importer hub file genuinely cannot take the `export =` form without a code change. That is a property of the file, not a time problem, and `CLAUDE.md` doesn't anticipate it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

# PO-S10 report

**20 of the 60 files are now TypeScript (3,979 of 16,966 lines); the other 40 are JavaScript, identical to `HEAD`.** The build passes, 375 tests pass, and the run finished 67 minutes after the start (limit 100). Thirty of the 40 do not fit the rules as written; only ten were left for time.

## Final build and test

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run build:server` | passes (the incremental build did not crash) |
| `npm test` | 375 passing |
| Whole-tree no-emit check | 0 errors |
| Compiled output, 449 files not converted | byte-identical to the baseline |
| Compiled output, 20 converted files | only require lines, comments and two export forms differ (listed below) |
| Banned constructs, counted from the syntax tree | 0 `any`, 0 `@ts-` comments, 0 `as unknown as` |

Two checks I added: each of the seven commits type-checks on its own (0 errors each), and loading `Server.js` from the baseline and from the new build loads the same 363 modules in the same order.

Commits, on top of `6752a047`, nothing pushed:

- `c717a73c` types: declare `semver`
- `19e5ff12` set 1
- `f5646086` set 6 (before set 2, because `CoverManager.ts` imports a type from `parseEbookMetadata.ts`)
- `6c52529a` set 2
- `8c3c7a36` set 3
- `b90bc8f4` set 4
- `3dfc6779` set 5

Timing: start 16:47, probe 16:49 to 17:02, sub-agents started 17:02, all six reported between 17:34 and 17:43, integration finished 17:54. No sub-agent had to be told to stop, and no file had to be restored at integration.

## Per set

| Set | Converted | Lines | Restored after a trial | Not started |

| 1 | 3 of 5 | 991 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 4 of 8 | 1,118 | 1 | 3 |

| 4 | 4 of 15 | 409 | 4 | 7 |
| 5 | 2 of 12 | 281 | 2 | 8 |
| 6 | 6 of 17 | 583 | 2 | 9 |
| **All** | **20 of 60** | **3,979** | **11** | **29** |

**Set 1.** Converted: `NotificationManager`, `CronManager`, `PlaybackSessionManager`.
- Restored: `RssFeedManager` — three values the original leaves unguarded (`feed.entity` after `getEntity()` twice, `feed` after `updateFeedForEntity()`).
- Not started: `PodcastManager` (time).

**Set 2.** Converted: `CoverSearchManager`, `CacheManager`, `MigrationManager`, `CoverManager`.
- Restored: `BinaryManager` — a null `platformSuffix` is used as an index, unguarded (line 157).
- Not started: `BackupManager` (time, and `req.files.file` is unguarded); `AudioMetadataManager` and `AbMergeManager` (every read of `task.data` would need a `!` and a cast from `unknown`, because the converted `Task.ts` types it `Record<string, unknown> | null`).

**Set 3.** Converted: `AudioFileScanner`.
- Restored: `LibraryScanner` — reads the untested `false` result of `getFileTimestampsWithIno()`, assigns a number to `Library.lastScan`, reads `libraryFolders` unguarded.
- Not started: `BookScanner` (time).

**Set 4.** Converted: `PodcastEpisodeDownload`, `LibraryScan`, `OpfFileScanner`, `AbsMetadataFileScanner`.
- Restored:
  - `MediaProbeData` — `audioStream` is dereferenced while it can be null.
  - `Backup` — `BackupController.ts:159` breaks once `fullPath` is `string | null`.
  - `LibraryFile` — the same untested `false` result.
  - `NfoFileScanner` — reads the converted `NfoMetadata` interface by a dynamic key.
- Not started, same kind of blocker: `AudioFile` (`AudioTrack.ts:42,47` reads `metadata` unguarded), `PlaybackSession`, `LibraryItemScanner`.
- Not started, time: `Stream`, `LibraryItemScanData`, `PodcastScanner`, `Scanner`.

**Set 5.** Converted: `profiler`, `comicBookExtractors`.
- Restored: `areEquivalent` (needs `any` for dynamic access on `unknown`); `zipHelpers` (the vendored `archiver` is not callable from TypeScript; only `as unknown as` compiles).
- Not started:
  - `index`, `fileUtils`, `podcastUtils` — module-level `this`, see below.
  - `rateLimiterFactory`, `scandir`, `prober`, `libraryHelpers`, `ffmpegHelpers` — each needs a `!` or cast on a value nothing guarantees.

**Set 6.** Converted: `MusicBrainz`, `GoogleBooks`, `CustomProviderAdapter`, `FantLab`, `opmlGenerator`, `parseEbookMetadata`.
- Restored: `parseNameString` (its real return type breaks `AuthorController.ts:143,209`); `Audnexus` (a variable assigned only in a callback narrows to `never`).
- Not started, does not fit: `Audible`, `iTunes`, `abmetadataGenerator`, `parseOverdriveMediaMarkers`, `parseOpfMetadata`, `parseComicMetadata`.
- Not started, time: `parseEpubMetadata`, `TokenManager`, `OidcAuthStrategy`.

## Counts

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `!` field set before it is read | 2 | 14 | 2 | 16 | 3 | 0 | **37** |

The totals (51 `!`, 6 index signatures, 54 casts) are my own count from the syntax tree and match the sub-agents' totals; the split into cases is theirs.

The 39 "other" casts:
- 19 `libs/fsExtra` missing methods
- 3 `libs/fsExtra` return types (`remove`, `copy`)
- 6 `LibraryItem.media` union
- 2 `libs/dateAndTime`
- 2 `abmetadataGenerator.parseJson`
- 2 Node `Module` internals
- 1 each: `libs/umzug`, `Sequelize.QueryTypes`, `sanitizeFilename`, a `getTrackList` argument, a `libarchive` argument

No `import type` replaces a require; five new type-only imports were added. Set 1 also uses four `Record<string, T>` types, not counted as index signatures.

**Compiled-output differences in the 20 files (16 lines):**
- `NotificationManager`, `MusicBrainz`, `GoogleBooks` and `FantLab` now read `require('axios').default`. This is the form of `OpenLibrary.ts`, and it is the same object on axios 0.27.2 (checked).
- `require('uuid').v4`, `require('package.json').version` and `libs/dateAndTime` are each split into a require plus a local const.
- `opmlGenerator` and `parseEbookMetadata` end with one `export =` instead of `module.exports.x = …`.
- `AudioFileScanner` no longer requires `../models/LibraryItem`, which it used only in JSDoc types.

## Where the sets affected each other

**In the final state: nowhere.** No file of one set is broken by another set's change.

During the run:
- **One real case, set 6 to set 3.** Set 6's trial of `parseNameString` (17:24) gave `AudioFileScanner.ts` two TS2322 errors at lines 352 and 354. They went away when set 6 restored its file.
- **Converted files outside the sets** were broken briefly by a file in progress, and each time the owning sub-agent fixed or restored its file:
  - `AuthorController.ts` — set 6 (`parseNameString` trial); also a "not a module" error from set 2's renames
  - `BackupController.ts` — set 4 (`Backup` trial)
  - `RSSFeedController.ts` — set 1 (`RssFeedManager` trial)
  - `LibraryController.ts` and `LibraryItemController.ts` — set 3
  - `ShareController.ts`, `HlsRouter.ts`, `PublicRouter.ts` — set 1
  - `AuthorFinder.ts`, `BookFinder.ts` — set 6
- **The effect I expected did not happen.** Set 5's `index.js` and `fileUtils.js` could not be converted, so they never changed types under the other sets.

Latent, for the next run (the consumers are still JavaScript, so nothing shows yet):
- `PodcastEpisodeDownload` fields are now nullable, which `PodcastManager` and `ffmpegHelpers` read directly.
- `LibraryScan.library` is now nullable, which `LibraryScanner` reads directly.
- `executeMediaFileScans()` returns `(AudioFile | null)[]`, which `BookScanner` and `PodcastScanner` read without a test.
- `parseEbookMetadata.ts` needs `BookScanner`'s typedef `BookMetadataObject` to stay importable.
- Four casts in converted controllers are no longer needed and their comments name JSDoc that is gone: `LibraryItemController.ts:365` and `:510`, `ShareController.ts:133`, `AuthorController.ts:448`.

## Did CLAUDE.md work as written?

**Yes, for what it covers.** No banned construct, no behaviour change, no file handed back with an error, and all 11 trial restores left an empty diff.

**Not covered, and it blocked files** (each needs your rule or decision):
1. **Module-level `this`.** `index.js`, `fileUtils.js`, `podcastUtils.js` and `parseOpfMetadata.js` call their own exports through `this` in top-level arrow functions (10 places in the first three). `export =` replaces `module.exports` with a new object, so those calls fail at runtime; set 5 reproduced it. They convert only if `this.` may become `module.exports.`, which is a code change. This blocks the two most-imported files of the run.
2. **A null-initialised field that a converted file reads unguarded** (`Backup`, `AudioFile`). No truthful type avoids breaking a file nobody may edit.
3. **A helper that returns `false` and is read untested** (`getFileTimestampsWithIno`, three files). `!` does not remove `false`.
4. **Reading a converted interface by a dynamic key** (`NfoFileScanner`). It needs an index signature in a converted file that is not a model.
5. **The vendored `archiver` is not callable** (`zipHelpers`, `BackupManager:435`). It needs a declaration in `server/libs/` or a ruling.
6. **Casts no allowance names:** a variable assigned only in a callback, a function that changes its argument's type in place, a too-vague return of a converted file (allowance 3 covers only arguments).

**Not covered, used by sub-agents, accepted by me** (please rule; each is a single-file restore if you disagree):
- **Wrong argument count (TS2554), in three forms:** an erased overload (`CronManager.ts:219`), a widening annotation of the local `axios` (`MusicBrainz.ts:3`), and a string type with a one-argument `replace` (`AudioFileScanner.ts:30`).
- **File-local redeclared built-ins:** `Number` (`PlaybackSessionManager`) and `Boolean` as a type guard (`AudioFileScanner`), modelled on the existing `isNaN` precedent, which CLAUDE.md does not list either.
- **`!` readings:**
  - the guarantee is a test in the callers (`NotificationManager.ts:244`, `CronManager.ts:100`, all 16 in set 4);
  - a property added right after creation (`profiler.ts:40`);
  - an include that is a left join (`CronManager.ts:173`).
- **Boundary casts at typed modules with a missing member** (`Sequelize.QueryTypes`, Node's `Module`), and at `fsExtra` return types.
- **The allowance-3 form at a JavaScript or `libs` callee** (`comicBookExtractors.ts:165`, `PlaybackSessionManager.ts:408`). The precedent is `LibraryController.ts:708`.
- **The `.default` read and the elided require** listed above.

**Process gaps:**
- The harness refused every sub-agent's `report.md`, so the six reports exist only as hand-back messages in this session. Each set's `bugs.md` and `declarations-needed.md` are in the scratchpad under `set1/` to `set6/`.
- A sub-agent cannot test a declaration it may not add. I gave each a private no-emit config with a `pending.d.ts`; set 2 used it for `semver`. A model declaration cannot be tested this way; none was needed.
- All six transpiled single files in their scratch folders to see compiled output, because the no-emit check cannot show it.
- The probe counts did not predict which files fit. Files failed on one to three null or `never` errors, not on the many implicit-any ones, and `checkJs` cannot show a conflict with a converted importer. My set briefs were too optimistic because of this.
- My set 5 brief named the wrong precedent for `module.exports.x` files (`requestUtils.ts` instead of `parseSeriesString.ts`). It did not change the outcome.

**Declarations:** I added `semver`, the only one a converted file needed. I did not add two that nothing needs yet: `embeddedCoverArt` on `Book.AudioFileObject` (set 2, optional) and `findOne`/`update` on `LibraryItemModelStatic` (set 3, for a later `LibraryScanner`, not compiled).
